subject: Network gating, smoke checklist & rollback criteria for private stack handoff
messages:

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T12:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network gating, smoke checklist & rollback criteria for private stack handoff

Danielle —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attaching the excerpted runbook and the guardrail policy (see attachments). Below is the concise checklist we will run during the handoff window and the explicit rollback conditions. This is the set we use for all Private (VPC/on-prem) cutovers — tuned for minimal blast radius.

Pre-cutover (T-24h)
- Confirm final config pushed to mdm-config (git tag: vpc-handoff/v1.2).
- Verify customer peering ASN and prefix filters (Aurora ASN 64512).
- Smoke CA cert issuance: create ephemeral cert and validate chain via our test CA endpoint.
- KMS key access test: encrypt/decrypt round trip with customer KMS role.
- Nightly snapshot of model artifacts present on storage nodes and checksums match.

Cutover window (canary + ramp)
- Step 1 (canary, 10m): route 5% production traffic through new nodes. Health criteria to continue:
  - 99.95% 200 responses on /v1/health for 10m window
  - P50 latency within expected baseline (+20ms tolerance)
  - No new 5xx errors > 0.5% of requests
- Step 2 (ramp, next 30-45m): increase to 50% then 100% with staged autoscale triggers.
- Network validations during ramp:
  - BGP session stable (no flaps) for 15m after each jump
  - Route propagation validated via route reflector and customer BGP view
  - Firewall stateful sessions preserved for long-lived flows (NAT mapping check)
- Observability checks:
  - Token-level cost meter sanity (no >30% sudden token spike)
  - KV cache hit rate within 10% of control baseline

Rollback (abort) criteria — immediate rollback if any of the following occur:
- Canary window: >0.5% new 5xx or sustained P95 latency increase >100ms
- BGP session loss for >2 minutes during ramp or route blackhole detected
- KMS access failures for key ops (encrypt/decrypt) affecting >5% of requests
- Critical telemetry gap (missing traces or missing ingestion for >10m)

Post-cutover validation (first 4h)
- Run full smoke suite (attached log) across multiple regions and persistence layers.
- Confirm audit logs for model loads and inference requests are landing in customer SIEM.
- Share a 1-hour and 4-hour summary with Aurora SRE and CS.

Attachments: vpc-handoff-runbook-v1.2.pdf, traffic-guardrail-policy.yaml

Rohan and Dylan — please confirm the BGP knobs and the NAT mapping test are in the runbook (I linked the exact commands under the related link). Any additions?

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Danielle Park <dpark@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-06T08:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network gating, smoke checklist & rollback criteria for private stack handoff

Adding two practical items we validated in staging that will be part of the handoff ops:

1) ARP/NAT warmup script: we will execute a NAT mapping probe (script attached in runbook) pre-cutover and after each routing jump. This ensures long-lived sessions (e.g., streaming inference) don't break when we flip IPs.

2) NTP/clock drift tolerance step: some of Aurora's on-prem boxes had >120s drift in staging. We'll run a forced NTP sync and verify cluster members report <5s drift before canary. If drift persists, we hold — that is a hard-block.

Also: we should set a short suppression window for non-actionable alerts (e.g., autoscale churn) to avoid noise during ramp. I'll own the alert suppression plan and the quick play to re-enable post-cutover.

-Rohan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Danielle Park <dpark@aurorahealth.com>

- Please confirm the exact CloudWatch / Prometheus metrics and the alert IDs you will be suppressing. We want to make sure our Ops team has matching suppressions.

Assuming the items above are clear, we can confirm the window: 2025-11-07 02:00–04:00 PT. We prefer earlier windows for lower traffic.

Thanks —
Danielle
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Park <dpark@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-07T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Network gating, smoke checklist & rollback criteria for private stack handoff — Post-deploy summary

Danielle —

Thanks for a smooth window overnight. Quick summary of execution and results (full smoke log attached — post-deploy-smoke-output-aurora.log):

Execution highlights:
- Canary (02:05–02:15 PT): 5% traffic for 10m; health passed. 200s at 99.98%, P50 +12ms vs baseline, no new 5xx >0.1%.
- Ramp to 50% then 100% completed by 02:55 PT. BGP stable, no flaps recorded. Route propagation verified from both sides.
- KMS encrypt/decrypt success rate 100% during and after ramp.
- NAT warmup: Aurora ran pre-seed script; we ran verification probes — mappings persisted through ramp.

Minor findings and follow-ups:
- Observability: one agent on a persistence host failed to report traces for a 7m window at 03:10. We captured the agent logs and restarted the exporter; metrics resumed. Root cause is a transient OOM — Dylan flagged for a sizing tweak in the next maintenance cycle (INFRA-4821).
- Telemetry: token cost meter showed an expected transient jump (18%) during artifact pulls; returned to baseline in 20m.

No rollback triggers hit. Per runbook we left alert suppression active for 1h post-ramp and then re-enabled. Attached are the runbook excerpt and the guardrail policy used.

Deliverables we shared with Aurora:
- 1-hour and 4-hour summary (this thread will serve as the 4-hour note)
- Full smoke output: post-deploy-smoke-output-aurora.log
- Change artifacts: vpc-handoff-runbook-v1.2.pdf, traffic-guardrail-policy.yaml

Next steps:
- Rohan to post sizing recommendation for exporter (ticket INFRA-4821).
- Naomi will schedule a 1-week ops sync to review any residual telemetry anomalies.

Thanks all — great execution team.

Naomi
Director, Customer Deployments — Redwood Inference
